name: How do I compare two pool renovation bids that look very different?

mainEntity.name: Why do pool renovation quotes vary so much, and how do I compare them?
mainEntity.text: Why do pool renovation quotes vary so much, and how do I compare them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Big price gaps usually mean the bids are not covering the same work. One quote may include full demolition, shell prep, tile, coping, equipment updates, permits, startup, and cleanup, while another may only price the obvious finish items. To compare properly, line up each estimate by category and check what is excluded. Material allowances also matter because a low allowance can make a quote look cheaper until upgrades are selected. Ask whether hidden repairs are included as a contingency or treated as separate change orders. It helps to normalize the bids by asking each contractor to restate the scope in the same format. A strong comparison focuses on completeness, not just headline price. In luxury markets, the cheapest bid can end up being the most expensive if it leaves out important repairs or finishes that must be added later. The best bid is the one that is clear, complete, and realistic.
acceptedAnswer.description: Pool renovation bids often differ because one contractor may include demolition, repairs, permits, equipment, and cleanup while another only prices the visible finish work. Compare scope, materials, exclusions, allowances, and warranty rather than just the total price.
